newsitem.title: USA: Packard Bell unveils $999 personal computer.
newsitem.headline: Packard Bell unveils $999 personal computer.

text.p: Packard Bell Corp., aiming at the family market for entry-level personal computers, said Friday it was launching a Pentium-based machine priced at $999, including a colour monitor.

The Packard Bell C115 will include a 120 MHz Pentium processor, 16 MB of EDO RAM, 1.2 GB hard drive, 8X CD-ROM, 33.6 Kbps modem/14.4 fax, a 14-inch colour monitor and a full communications package with a telephone answering system and a full-duplex speakerphone, the company said.
The model, now available in retail outlets, will also be sold without a monitor.

The Sacramento-based company cited a report by International Data Corp. that said nearly two-thirds of American households do not own a personal computer. The average $2,000 price tag, as well as a lack of understanding about the need for investing in a personal computer, were two reasons cited in the IDC report, it said.
"Our vision is to make a personal computer affordable for every home," said Beny Alagem, chairman, president and chief executive of Packard Bell NEC Inc.
"By providing an entry-level PC from a top manufacturer in the sub-$1,000 price range, Packard Bell will help non-users take that first step to PC ownership," he said.
Packard Bell is owned by Japan's NEC Corp.
